rationale: The unit opens on the header that begins Agur's collection, דִּבְרֵ֤י ... הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א (oshb:Prov.30.1, "the words of Agur ... the oracle"), and runs through a first-person meditation on the limits of human knowledge before God (30:2-4) into an affirmation that God's own word is tested and trustworthy (30:5) and a warning not to add to it, אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל דְּבָרָ֑יו (oshb:Prov.30.6, "do not add to his words"). The skeleton דִּבְרֵ֤י occurs in 19 verses book-wide (sweep: 19), of which 9 are genuine construct-state "words of X" forms (1.6, 12.6, 18.4, 18.8, 22.12, 22.17, 26.22, 30.1, 31.1); the remaining 10 are pronominal-suffixed ("my/your/his words": 1.23, 4.4, 4.20, 23.8, 29.20, 30.6) or absolute-plural ("words": 10.19, 24.26, 26.6, 29.19) forms of the same root. Of the 19, the construct form opens the verse in 5 (sweep: 5 of 19, the verse-initial subset), and pairs with an oracle-word to form an actual collection header in only 2 of those 5 (sweep: 2 of 5) -- here and again at the Lemuel header. The petuchah recorded at oshb:Prov.30.6 (single-witness) corroborates this seam before the numbered petition that begins the next unit.
rejected_alternative: Splitting the divrei/massa header (30:1) into its own row was considered, since it alone carries the disputed Ithiel-Ucal reading, but the first-person voice of 30:1 continues without interruption into the confession of 30:2, so the header stays inside the unit it opens.
observed_substrate_signals: verse-initial header token דִּבְרֵ֤י paired with הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א at oshb:Prov.30.1
the doubled name-form לְאִֽיתִיאֵ֑ל לְאִ֖יתִיאֵ֣ל וְאֻכָֽל at oshb:Prov.30.1 (the Ithiel/Ucal crux; disclosed, reading not resolved here)
imperative closing warning אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל דְּבָרָ֑יו at oshb:Prov.30.6
petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.6 (single-witness) closing the unit
the confession spanning 30:2-5 opens without a numeral or vocative-address formula, unlike the numbered sayings later in the chapter
device_notes: Register is first-person confessional (30:2-5) framed by third-person narration about the speaker (30:1) and a second-person warning (30:6) -- parallelism class synthetic; descriptive texture, not the unit_type choice. Greek witnesses relocate this material: Agur's opening block (30:1-14, including this row's own span) relocates after 24:22 in Greek order; Agur's numerical sayings (30:15-33) relocate together with Lemuel's oracle (31:1-9) after 24:34; the eshet-chayil acrostic (31:10-31) remains at the book's end -- a cross-tradition fact about Greek ordering that does not bear on the MT/WEB boundaries argued in this span, which agree on one consistent order across chs 30-31.

rationale: A new petition formula opens with the numeral שְׁ֭תַּיִם (oshb:Prov.30.7, "two things"), distinct in voice and grammar from the confession that precedes it -- the petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.6 (single-witness, disclosed) marks that seam. The petition is unpacked through a request to be free of falsehood and of both poverty and riches (30:8), reasoned in 30:9 with a rhetorical question naming the divine name directly, מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה (oshb:Prov.30.9, "who is Yahweh"), the sole occurrence of that exact token in this chapter (sweep: 1 of 70 book-wide). The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.9 (single-witness, disclosed) closes the petition before the unrelated servant/slander saying that follows.
rejected_alternative: Merging 30:7-9 into the preceding Agur unit was considered, since both are first-person material separated only by a non-driver petuchah at 30:6, but 30:7 shifts to a direct 2nd-person petition addressed to God, distinct from 30:1-6's 3rd-person narration (30:1) and 1st-person confession before God (30:2-5) plus 2nd-person warning to a human audience (30:6) -- the register shift, not the shared mark, is the seam's real warrant.
observed_substrate_signals: divine-name question מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה at oshb:Prov.30.9
petuchah brackets both ends of the unit (oshb:Prov.30.6 and oshb:Prov.30.9, both single-witness)
device_notes: The two-thing opening here anticipates the three/four formulas used later in the chapter's nature sayings, but unpacks two petitions rather than an itemized list of nouns -- texture distinguishing this saying's shape from the animal-list sayings, not a separate unit_type.

rationale: The chapter's second three/four formula opens the unit, שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה ... וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה (oshb:Prov.30.18, "three ... four"; the "four" token sits as an unpointed ketiv וארבע directly before its pointed qere וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה, disclosed). Its fourth listed item -- "the way of a man with a maiden" -- is picked up by an explicit catchword chain: the noun for "way" opens all four items of 30:19 and is used a fifth time to open the comparison verse itself, כֵּ֤ן דֶּ֥רֶךְ אִשָּׁ֗ה (oshb:Prov.30.20), “So is the way of an adulterous woman” (web:Prov.30.20). The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.17 (single-witness, disclosed) opens the unit and the petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.20 (single-witness, disclosed) closes it.
rejected_alternative: Setting 30:20 apart as an independent proverb about adultery was considered, since its subject differs from the nature-list of 30:19, but the fifth repetition of the same "way" noun ties it to the list as the formula's own application rather than a new topic.
observed_substrate_signals: three/four numeral pair שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה/וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה at oshb:Prov.30.18 (ketiv/qere verse; the K/Q pair itself is the next signal)
"way" (דֶּ֤רֶךְ) catchword opens all four list items (4 of 4) in oshb:Prov.30.19 and reopens oshb:Prov.30.20
petuchah brackets both ends, oshb:Prov.30.17 and oshb:Prov.30.20 (both single-witness)
device_notes: Parallelism class synthetic (list plus applied analogy); the repeated "way" noun is the cluster's own catchword-chain evidence.

rationale: The unit opens on the book's second and final divrei-plus-massa header, דִּ֭בְרֵי לְמוּאֵ֣ל מֶ֑לֶךְ מַ֝שָּׂ֗א (oshb:Prov.31.1, "the words of Lemuel the king, an oracle"), matching web:Prov.30.1 in kind (the same opening token דִּ֭בְרֵי pairs with an oracle-word as an actual header in 2 of the 19 book-wide hits, sweep: 2 of 19) though never in wording. The mother's address that follows opens with a triple vocative on a short root, מַה בְּ֭רִי וּמַֽה בַּר בִּטְנִ֑י וּ֝מֶה בַּר נְדָרָֽי (oshb:Prov.31.2, "what, my son! what, son of my womb! what, son of my vows!") -- the later two vocatives here, בַּר and בַּר, use a short form beside the fuller בְּ֭רִי used earlier in the same verse; that short form is Aramaic-influenced address vocabulary, discussion material rather than a claim that the verse itself is in Aramaic (every morph code in the book is H-prefixed, sweep: 6984 of 6984). The same address continues through the warnings against wine and women (31:3-7, including the twice-repeated אַ֤ל לַֽמְלָכִ֨ים לְֽמוֹאֵ֗ל אַ֣ל לַֽמְלָכִ֣ים at oshb:Prov.31.4, ketiv/qere verse, "not for kings ... not for kings") into the closing charge to judge the poor justly (31:8-9); the petuchah at oshb:Prov.31.9 (single-witness, disclosed) is the unit's one interior mark, closing it right before the acrostic begins.
rejected_alternative: Splitting the wine warning (31:3-7) from the justice charge (31:8-9) into two admonition_unit rows was considered, since their imagery differs, but across 31:2-8, four of the seven verses carry the mother's direct singular address (31:2 vocative address; 31:3 2ms prohibition; 31:4 vocative לְֽמוֹאֵ֗ל (oshb:Prov.31.4, ketiv/qere verse) plus infinitive; 31:8 2ms imperative), while three depart from it within the same wine-warning topic (31:5, 31:7: 3ms narrative describing an unnamed king-figure; 31:6: 2mp imperative to a different addressee) -- the one-unit reading holds on the petuchah bracket (oshb:Prov.30.33 and oshb:Prov.31.9, both single-witness) and the address-envelope spanning 31:2 to 31:8, not on uniform address verse by verse.
observed_substrate_signals: triple bar/beri vocative מַה בְּ֭רִי וּמַֽה בַּר בִּטְנִ֑י וּ֝מֶה בַּר נְדָרָֽי at oshb:Prov.31.2
repeated prohibition אַ֤ל לַֽמְלָכִ֨ים at oshb:Prov.31.4 (ketiv/qere verse), tokens 0-1 and 3-4
petuchah closing the unit at oshb:Prov.31.9 (single-witness)
device_notes: Parallelism class synthetic instruction (vocative, prohibition, counter-command, charge). The ketiv/qere at oshb:Prov.31.4 (disclosed) sits inside the wine-prohibition clause, an unpointed short form before its pointed counterpart, the same unpointed-before-pointed shape recorded at oshb:Prov.30.10.
